notesStmt.note: The corrections on this slip were almost certainly made sometime in 1889.

A corrected proof slip of "To Be Present Only," Whitman's response to an invitation to give an address at the complimentary dinner held in honor of his 70th birthday in Camden, New Jersey, on 31 May 1889. Horace Traubel published Whitman's response as "At the Complimentary Dinner, Camden, New Jersey, May 31, 1889 " in Camden's Compliment to Walt Whitman, May 31, 1889: Notes, Addresses, Letters, Telegrams (Philadelphia: David McKay, 1889). Whitman later collected this response in Complete Prose Works (1892), under the title "To Be Present Only." Whitman was in the habit of ordering batches of specially printed proof slips that he then "corrected" in small ways and presented as mementos to friends and admirers. The present manuscript seems to be one such document, as another nearly identical slip is extant. Also extant is a draft of the slip, with directions to the printer, in which Whitman requests "25 copies / good paper."

head.hi:
At the Complimentary Dinner, Camden,
New Jersey, May 31, 1889.

body.p: Walt Whitman said: My friends, though announced to give an address, there is no such intention.

Following the impulse of the spirit, (for I am at least half of Quaker stock) I have obeyed the command to come and look at you, my friends, for a minute, and show myself, face to face; which is probably the best I can do. But I have felt no command to make a speech; and shall not therefore attempt any. All I have felt the imperative conviction to say I have already printed in my books of poems or prose; to which I refer any who may be curious. And so, hail and farewell. Deeply acknowledging this deep compliment, with my best respects and love to you personally—to Camden—to New-Jersey, and to all represented here—you must excuse me from any word further.
